Police and Heroes.text: Japan's police and its heroes divide the work of public safety. Heroes respond to Quirk crimes, disasters and rescues, and they restrain villains with their Quirks. Police officers do not use their Quirks as weapons on duty; they secure scenes, investigate crimes, take statements, collect evidence, make formal arrests and hold suspects in custody. A hero's capture becomes a case only when the police take over: an officer makes the arrest, the hero gives a statement and the evidence enters the police chain of custody, never the hero's keeping. Heroes may not hold or interrogate suspects on their own. Cooperation works best at the local level, where patrol heroes and police stations know each other by name. For larger operations the police and agencies plan together: detectives build the case, then request heroes for the arrest, with a lead hero and a police commander sharing command. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi, a familiar face around Musutafu, is one of the officers heroes most often work with. Friction exists. Heroes collect the headlines and the case credit while detectives do the slow work; police complain about heroes who wreck evidence, chase suspects across jurisdictions or treat officers as a cleanup crew; heroes complain about paperwork and slow warrants. The Hero Public Safety Commission coordinates heroes and police at the national level, and in daily practice most officers and pros respect each other's limits.
